title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: all employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies
tiers.description: All directors and employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies. Restricted only by the insider trading prohibition, plus the standalone ban on derivatives over unvested or restricted securities which applies to any employee holding such securities. No trading window or clearance requirement applies to this tier.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors; all Executive Leadership Team members; all direct reports to Executive Leadership Team members; all BlueScope Steel Executives; all employees having access to the monthly consolidated financial information; and other employees as nominated from time to time. Subject to the trading windows, the written clearance requirement, the nine month short-term trading ban and the ban on new pledging arrangements.

tiers.name: Controlled Entities
tiers.description: In relation to an employee or director, an entity in relation to which the employee or director has investment control in respect of dealings in BlueScope Steel securities. The employee or director must ensure the Controlled Entity trades only in accordance with the Policy and as if it were itself a Restricted Person.

tiers.name: Family Members
tiers.description: Spouses and children who are co-resident with the employee or director. A Restricted Person must take reasonable steps to ensure they trade only in a trading window and otherwise in accordance with the Policy.

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security

windows.start_anchor: commencement of trading the day following the announcement of the half year results
commencement of trading the day following the announcement of the full year results
commencement of the trading day following the Annual General Meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, in its absolute discretion, considers current and expected corporate activity prior to the scheduled opening of each trading window and determines whether to modify that window for any Restricted Person or group of Restricted Persons; it may also open a special trading window. The policy does not say whether a modification is announced or kept confidential.

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading; Trading by Restricted Persons; Requirements before trading
rules.detail: A 'cap or collar facility' is expressly named as a form of restricted trading rather than as a prohibited transaction. It is therefore permitted for a Restricted Person if entered into inside a trading window, after written notification to the Company Secretary, confirmation of no inside information and written advice that there is no known reason to preclude the trading. Third party put and call options over BlueScope Steel securities are separately named, so both legs of a collar are covered.
rules.evidence: entering into any other form of derivative contract relating to a security, such as a cap or collar facility; and any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security.

rules.tier: all employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies
rules.section: Employees covered by this policy; Insider trading is prohibited at all times
rules.detail: The trading windows and clearance requirement are imposed only on Restricted Persons. An employee outside that group who holds no unvested or restricted securities may enter a derivative over BlueScope Steel securities subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: This policy imposes trading restrictions on all employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies who are in possession of inside information, and additional trading restrictions on the following people in BlueScope Steel and its related companies (Restricted Persons)

rules.section: No derivatives over unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities
rules.detail: Flat ban on derivatives and any risk-limiting transaction over unvested securities, applying to every employee and not only Restricted Persons, with no clearance route. The ban expressly extends to transactions managing the risk of the timing, likelihood or manner of vesting.
rules.evidence: not enter any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities. This includes not entering any transaction to manage the risk of the timing, likelihood or manner of vesting, or unrestricted vesting, of any unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities.

rules.section: No derivatives over unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities
rules.detail: 'Restricted' securities are treated identically to unvested ones, so shares that have vested but remain within a restriction period cannot be hedged at all. The short-term trading section confirms that a restriction period is a distinct state which ends before the securities become freely dealable.
rules.evidence: Employees who hold unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities must: comply with the terms of issue of those securities; and not enter any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities.

rules.section: No derivatives over unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities
rules.detail: Rationale given is that hedging would distort the proper functioning of performance hurdles and reduce alignment between management and shareholder interests. No exceptions and no approver.
rules.evidence: The use of derivative contracts in relation to unvested or restricted securities could distort the proper functioning of performance hurdles and reduce the intended alignment between management and shareholder interests.

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading
rules.detail: Hedging vested unrestricted securities is not banned. 'Any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security' appears in the list of restricted trading, meaning it is a trade requiring a trading window and written clearance, not a prohibited act. This is the pivotal drafting choice in the policy.
rules.evidence: any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security.

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading
rules.detail: Forward trading is expressly listed as restricted trading, so a prepaid forward or forward sale over vested unrestricted securities is permitted within a trading window with written clearance. A monetisation that pledges the securities is separately caught by the forced sale section.
rules.evidence: short or forward trading any security or financial product listed above

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading; No short-term trading
rules.detail: Short trading is listed as restricted trading rather than prohibited, so on the face of the policy it requires a trading window and clearance. In practice a short position closed within nine months would breach the short-term trading ban.
rules.evidence: short or forward trading any security or financial product listed above

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere and does not appear in the list of restricted trading or in the forced sale section.

rules.section: Restrictions extend to all forms of securities and trading
rules.detail: Contracts for difference are not named but fall within 'any other form of derivative contract relating to a security', so they are restricted trading requiring a window and clearance for a Restricted Person. Over unvested or restricted securities a CFD would be prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: entering into any other form of derivative contract relating to a security, such as a cap or collar facility

rules.section: Transactions that may involve a forced sale of BlueScope Steel securities
rules.detail: Margin lending is not named by that term, but a margin loan is the paradigm arrangement under which securities are pledged as collateral for a loan that could permit a sale without the holder's consent, and is therefore prohibited for Restricted Persons. The ban is prospective only: it bites on 'new arrangements' entered into from the date the section took effect.
rules.evidence: From the date this section takes effect, Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangements under which their BlueScope Steel securities are pledged as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent.

rules.section: Transactions that may involve a forced sale of BlueScope Steel securities
rules.detail: Conditional prohibition: the trigger is not the security interest itself but the possibility of a sale without the security holder's consent. A pledge under which the holder retains an absolute veto over any disposal is not caught on the wording, and the prohibition is not framed as a trade requiring clearance, so no approval route exists.
rules.evidence: must not enter into any new arrangements under which their BlueScope Steel securities are pledged as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent.

rules.tier: all employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies
rules.detail: The forced sale section is confined to Restricted Persons; the policy says nothing about pledging by other employees.

rules.section: Transactions that may involve a forced sale of BlueScope Steel securities; Trading outside the windows in special circumstances
rules.detail: The scope is any 'loan or other agreement' collateralised by BlueScope Steel securities, not just margin loans, and it captures the loan leg of a funded collar wherever the bank has an enforcement power of sale. There is no clearance or exemption route, and the special circumstances relief is expressly closed to trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of the policy.
rules.evidence: Exceptions will not be considered in the case of trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of this policy.

rules.detail: Nine month holding period on the same securities, illustrated by a worked example (shares bought 1 January may not be sold until 2 October). Only carve-out is the sale of securities after the vesting of share rights or the end of a restriction period.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this policy 'short-term' is defined as within a 9 month period. Accordingly, any dealing in the same BlueScope Steel securities within a 9 month period is prohibited.

clearance.approver: Company Secretary for trading inside a window; the Chairman (request made through the Company Secretary) for trading outside a window; the Board through the Company Secretary in the case of the Chairman
clearance.section: Requirements before trading; Trading outside the windows in special circumstances
clearance.evidence: The approval to trade in BlueScope Steel securities is valid for 10 trading days from the time the approval is given, and may be revoked at any time. If the proposed dealing in the securities does not occur within this 10 trading day period, the approval lapses and must be reapplied for.

clearance.tier: all employees of BlueScope Steel and its related companies
clearance.evidence: Restricted Persons are only permitted to trade BlueScope Steel securities: during the specific "trading windows" detailed below; and if they have notified the Company Secretary in writing in advance and received clearance

short_term.basis: any dealing in the same BlueScope Steel securities within a 9 month period
carve_outs: the sale of BlueScope Steel securities after the vesting of share rights or the end of a restriction period
short_term.evidence: This does not restrict the sale of BlueScope Steel securities after the vesting of share rights or the end of a restriction period.

exceptions.approver: Chairman, in writing, on a request made through the Company Secretary; the Board through the Company Secretary in the case of the Chairman
exceptions.evidence: Restricted Persons are prohibited from trading in BlueScope Steel securities at times outside the trading windows, however if a genuine and pressing requirement for funds causes a need to sell BlueScope Steel securities, then exceptions may be considered.
Exceptions will not be considered in the case of trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of this policy.

participation in share plans offered by the Company, provided the election to participate in the relevant plan is made during a trading window (this does not permit trading in shares acquired under Company share plans outside of trading windows); the exercise of vested share rights
trading under an offer made to all or most security holders (e.g. a rights issue, dividend re-investment plan or share buy-back).

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance. The operative test is consent: the ban catches any pledge as collateral for a loan or other agreement 'which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent', so the question for a bank is whether its security package confers any independent power of sale rather than whether the facility has a price trigger.

external_documents: Terms of issue of unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities under the Company's share plans
exemption_authority: The Chairman may give written clearance for a Restricted Person to trade outside a trading window where a genuine and pressing requirement for funds causes a need to sell; requests go through the Company Secretary, and for the Chairman to the Board through the Company Secretary. Clearance is valid for 10 trading days from the day after approval. The Board may modify a scheduled trading window or open a special trading window. No authority exists to waive the ban on derivatives over unvested or restricted securities or the pledging ban.

bespoke_clauses.topic: collar named as restricted trading, not prohibited
bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into any other form of derivative contract relating to a security, such as a cap or collar facility; and any other transaction that limits the economic risk of holding a security.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: BlueScope names a collar facility in the list of what counts as trading rather than in a prohibition, so the derivative legs of a collar over vested unrestricted shares are available to a Restricted Person inside a trading window with written clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: From the date this section takes effect, Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangements under which their BlueScope Steel securities are pledged as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This defeats the funded leg of a conventional collar loan, because a bank's security over the collared shares almost always includes an enforcement power of sale that does not require the holder's consent.

bespoke_clauses.clause: which could permit a sale of those securities without the security holder's consent
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is conditional, so a facility with no independent power of sale (cash settlement only, or security requiring the executive to direct any disposal) may fall outside it, and this is the drafting point to negotiate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Exceptions will not be considered in the case of trading resulting from a forced sale in breach of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a bank ever enforced, the executive would be in breach with no available cure, and breach is expressly a disciplinary matter that may include termination.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any dealing in the same BlueScope Steel securities within a 9 month period is prohibited
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: One of the longest short-term bans in the market: a collar over recently acquired shares, or one whose physical settlement occurs within nine months of the underlying purchase, would breach it, so tenor must exceed nine months and the underlying shares must be seasoned.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the 45 day periods from the commencement of trading the day following the announcement of the half year results and the day following the announcement of the full year results; and the 15 day period from the commencement of the trading day following the Annual General Meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Restricted Persons may deal only inside roughly 105 days a year, so collar entry, any roll and any physical settlement must all be scheduled into a window, and the Board may narrow a window before it opens.

bespoke_clauses.topic: ten trading day clearance with revocation
bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval to trade in BlueScope Steel securities is valid for 10 trading days from the time the approval is given, and may be revoked at any time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A comparatively long execution window for documenting and pricing a collar, but the bank cannot treat clearance as irrevocable up to signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: if a genuine and pressing requirement for funds causes a need to sell BlueScope Steel securities, then exceptions may be considered
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Out-of-window relief is framed around a need to sell, so it is doubtful the Chairman could use it to authorise entry into a collar or a financing outside a window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Employees who hold unvested or restricted BlueScope Steel securities must ... not enter any transaction that limits the economic risk of holding unvested or restricted securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedgeable pool is limited to shares that have vested and whose restriction period has ended; this ban applies to every employee, not only Restricted Persons, and has no clearance route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An employee or director must ensure that any Controlled Entity ... does not trade in BlueScope Steel securities except in accordance with this Policy (and as if the Controlled Entity itself was a Restricted Person).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A family trust or investment company used to hold the collared shares is treated as a Restricted Person in its own right, so the window, clearance and pledging rules follow the shares.

summary: A funded collar is close to workable at BlueScope but is defeated by the financing leg as ordinarily documented. The derivative legs are unusually accommodating: the policy names a 'cap or collar facility' and third party put and call options in the list of restricted trading rather than in a prohibition, so a Restricted Person may enter a collar over vested, unrestricted shares provided it is done inside one of the three trading windows (45 days after each of the half year and full year results, and 15 days after the AGM), after written notice to the Company Secretary, confirmation of no inside information and written clearance, which is valid for 10 trading days and revocable at any time. The loan leg is the problem: Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangement pledging BlueScope Steel securities as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale without the holder's consent, with no clearance route and no exemption authority, and any resulting forced sale is a breach for which exceptions will expressly not be considered. The prohibition is conditional rather than absolute, so a structure in which the bank has no independent power of sale over the collared shares is the only route worth exploring. Two further constraints apply: nothing may be hedged while unvested or within a restriction period, and the nine month short-term trading ban means the collar tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares must both exceed nine months.
